newsitem.title: USA: US Labor's Hamel-construction job drop due weather.
newsitem.headline: US Labor's Hamel-construction job drop due weather.

text.p: An economist with the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics said Friday that March job losses in the construction sector were due in part to cold weather.
"Unseasonably cold weather throughout most of the country partly explains the declines in construction," BLS Economist Harvey Hamel said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Hamel said he was not worried about the drop in the jobless rate to 4.9 percent from 5.2 percent the month before.
"I don't think it's a disturbing number," Hamel said. He noted that the unemployment rate had remained in a narrow range in the prior 10 ten months.
"You have to look to see if a trend develops," he said. "Unemployment is certainly low -- I'm not sure anyone needs to worry about a decline of three-tenths (of a point) in April."
The last time the unemployment rate stood at 4.9 percent was in December 1973. Many financial market participants fear low unemployment could unleash inflationary pressures.
